I feel like the game just didn't maintain the right tone to have such shocking moments carry any weight as the series moved forward. Modern Warfare 2 seemed to be the worst offender because the game had the lead characters literally commit war crimes and does nothing to show just how morally ambiguous (if we're being generous) such actions are. In Call of Duty 4 Price executes a captive, but at least in the context of what that captive had done and why you can understand why Price did it, even if it is morally wrong. By the time MW2 rolls around we have undercover CIA operatives mowing down civilians, a joint task force launching an all out assault on a densely populated favela, and all manner of other such things, and nothing has really changed except the actions being taken by the all too generic terrorist group have lost their weight . The only real explanation for such extreme measures is a lot of hand waving about bringing a single villain to justice, despite the fact that the way the protagonists go about it ends up inciting a global conflict, only to be resolved by Price killing Makarov himself rather than doing anything to make him stand trial. The whole series by this point feels less like fighting you're fighting a relentless and brutal foe with the best intentions, an more like you ARE the relentless and brutal foe you were so damn quick to compromise your values in fighting. It's a classic "the ends justify the means" approach that serves as just lazy writing at best, and is one of the many reasons why the series has gotten so repetitive.
